text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. To help localize the issue, does the weakness or numbness affect your thumbs and index fingers more than your pinkies, and do you notice any difficulty with fine motor tasks like buttoning shirts?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of fasciculations and absent reflexes is highly concerning for lower motor neuron involvement, such as Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis or a severe cervical myelopathy. REQUEST TEST: Cervical MRI

text: Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, hypertension, history of a motor vehicle accident 3 years prior. Social history: 7 sexual partners, uses condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI showing a syrinx is the key finding, and your symptoms of cape-like sensory loss and lower motor neuron signs fit perfectly with Syringomyelia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Syringomyelia
